pr_title: TSDB: Implement Downsampling ILM Action for time-series indices
pr_comment: Hi @csoulios, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

@dakrone thanks  a lot for the feedback.

> How will this work with an ILM policy? I looked at the implementation in TransportRollupAction, but it doesn't look like all of the metadata pieces get copied over. Right now that would mean that the down-sampling would happen but the new index is subject to templates for its settings.

Source indices are always deleted at the end of the rollup action and they are replaced by the rollup index. When an index belongs to a data stream, the souce index is replaced by the rollup index in the data stream too. This all happens at the [`TransportRollupAction`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/f64c75dca608760c0470896316c3aa81ade93845/x-pack/plugin/rollup/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/rollup/v2/TransportRollupAction.java#L567-L584).

You are right that not all the metadata pieces get copied over. We only copy the metadata required for the rollup process. 

Do you think that we should copy all metadata or copying only `index.lifecycle.name` is enough? 

>That means that the new index will need to have a separate template with a separate policy (since no rollover is needed), and that the new index will essentially "restart" its ILM lifecycle. This seems a little complicated to try and understand for an end user. I would imagine the simpler behavior is to pretend that rolling up the index is transparent and happens to the existing index (kind of like shrink) and then it goes its merry way along the rest of its lifecycle.

I absolutely agree with you. So, the rollup index should inherit the ILM policy of the source index (like a shrinked index inherits the ILM policy of the source index).

> In the old version we explicitly call out a new policy for the index to follow (and I think we all agreed that was very complicated), this is still kind of that, but even more confusing to a user since they'll need to set up a template beforehand.

That's correct. We want to avoid all complications of a separate ILM policy. This is why I removed the `rollup_policy` configuration param from the `rollup` action.

Finally, I was hoping I could copy the ILM related metadata in a different ILM step. However, this seems to be impossible since the source index has been deleted. Is there any way we can read index metadata before the `RollupStep` and somehow apply them after the `RollupStep` has completed? If that's not possible, I will probably need to copy metadata in the `RollupTransportAction`

> Well, I think it's okay to not support aliases directly, considering that an index will already be in TSDB-mode anyway, and that requires a data stream. What I am concerned about is if a user manually adds an index into a set of aliases, then when it is downsampled it gets automatically removed from those aliases. If the Rollup API is going to treat the downsample as a 1-to-1 replacement, it seems like it should also copy over the alias configuration so that it matches the previous index exactly.

I think this is not a problem? This feature only works with data streams and it is not allowed to create an alias that refers to a backing index of a data stream. A validation error should occur when such alias is attempted to be created. So I think we don't need to copy over the alias metadata.

@dakrone 

My initial intention was to make the `/<index/_rollup/<rollup-index>` action perform all required steps to rollup the index, delete the source and update the data stream. We (the team) have discussed your approach again in the past. However, thinking of it again, I start to like this solution for the following reasons:

- It keeps rollup behavior consistent with the shrink action
- We had a feeling that `TransportRollupAction` does too much and may have trouble with random failures. ILM seems to deal with failures better.
- We allow users to rollup an index without deleting the original source. This has been requested more than a few times already.


Let me discuss this approach with the team and I will get back to you

@dakrone I have addressed all points you commented on your review. 

1. Copy all source index metadata to the rollup index: Probably, this will happen in the `RollupTransportAction` and will not be part of the ILM action. I will implement this in a following PR.


2. @martijnvg mentioned: 

> I think this is not a problem? This feature only works with data streams and it is not allowed to create an alias that refers to a backing index of a data stream. A validation error should occur when such alias is attempted to be created. So I think we don't need to copy over the alias metadata.

So, I don't need toI add the `SwapAliasesAndDeleteSourceIndexStep` to make sure that aliases to the source index are transfered to the rollup index. Do I?

> > I think this is not a problem? This feature only works with data streams and it is not allowed to create an alias that refers to a backing index of a data stream. A validation error should occur when such alias is attempted to be created. So I think we don't need to copy over the alias metadata.
> 
> So, I don't need to add the `SwapAliasesAndDeleteSourceIndexStep` to make sure that aliases to the source index are transfered to the rollup index. Do I?

I had some doubts about this statement: "A validation error should occur when such alias is attempted to be created.", so I tested it and it looks that it's perfectly fine to create a concrete index (not belonging to a data stream) and assign an alias to it. And to be honest, I don't see the reason why why we should not allow it. 


```
curl http://localhost:9200/_cat/aliases
alias-KMcpC index-umvxyolteg - - - -

curl  http://localhost:9200/alias-KMcpC/_settings
{"index-umvxyolteg":{"settings":{"index":{"lifecycle":{"name":"policy-lGnYO","rollover_alias":"alias-KMcpC"},"mode":"time_series","routing":{"allocation":{"include":{"_tier_preference":"data_content"}}},"number_of_shards":"1","time_series":{"end_time":"2106-01-08T23:40:53.384Z","start_time":"2006-01-08T23:40:53.384Z"},"provided_name":"index-umvxyolteg","creation_date":"1657635048199","number_of_replicas":"0","routing_path":["metricset"],"uuid":"ZTUBnfr3TYyfn2uOPuZBvw","version":{"created":"8040099"}}}}}
```

So, in light of those findings, I should add the `SwapAliasesAndDeleteSourceIndexStep` to the list of actions.

Added `SwapAliasesAndDeleteSourceIndexStep` step in commit: [6c90a7a](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/87269/commits/6c90a7a9a5f3a7311ad76ccdecce1c9487eae441)

review_comment: Out of curiosity, why do we need to ensure that the lifecycle date is set here?

I don't have a good answer for this. I only copied it from the [`ShrinkStep`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/be7c7415627377a1b795400fb8dfcc6cbdf0e322/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/ilm/ShrinkStep.java#L62-L65) thinking this may be needed later since`ShrinkStep` and `RollupStep` are pretty similar in their operation.

Do you think I should remove this check?
No I don't think it's necessarily a bad check, I was just curious where it came from.
I can modify `ShrinkAction` so that it uses `CleanupTargetIndexStep` instead of `CleanupShrinkIndexStep` in a subsequent PR
Should these tests also perform a simple query to ensure that they can query the data stream without any problems after the rollup?

I added an assertion that the `IndexMetadata.INDEX_ROLLUP_STATUS` index setting is `RollupTaskStatus.SUCCESS` at the end of the process: [7345a57](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/87269/commits/7345a57ff42b461904e0722171298f935fad92f7)

For queries on rollup indexes there is the [`RollupActionSingleNodeTests` class](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/rollup/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/rollup/v2/RollupActionSingleNodeTests.java) that validates the result of the rollup action.

Now that I have removed the copy-settings step from rollup ILM action, I can revert the `CopySettingsStep` so that it uses `indexPrefix`. 

I only thought that making it more generic using an index name supplier function may be needed in the future. I don't have a strong opinion about keeping it this way or reverting it.
I think it's fine to keep for now
